assertions.name: Resonance prediction has correct sign (negative if Δ(q₀) > 3)

description: Benzene resonance energy as the Alexander-weight residual between Kekulé (3 localised T(2,2)) and threading T(2,6) encodings, multiplied by the molecular crossing-energy quantum.
caveats: At the substrate value q₀ ≈ 1.11, Δ_{T(2,6)}(q₀) > 3, so the weight difference is small and negative — predicting that the threading link is slightly *less* favourable than three localised double bonds, contrary to the experimental stabilisation of ~150 kJ/mol.  This is consistent with the manuscript's assertion that the resonance comes not from the single-link Alexander weight but from the *coherent* delocalisation of all 6 carbons in the threading link (prop:threading-half-weight).  A quantitative match awaits either (a) inclusion of the bond-order energy term (prop:bond-order-energy-formula, C13) or (b) an independent derivation of |q+q⁻¹|_mol that does not underpredict by factor ~5.
